name: OpenAI API & Agents Developer
audience: Developers with Python or TypeScript experience who build apps and agents on the OpenAI API
format: This site's course with a 40-question practice test in 60 minutes. OpenAI has no public developer certification.
verifyNotes: This is the site's own course; OpenAI has no public developer certification. Verify every API fact against developers.openai.com/api/docs and the Agents SDK docs: current models and reasoning effort, Responses API output items and conversation state, tool_choice, built-in tools and remote MCP, Structured Outputs strict-mode rules, Agents SDK primitives, caching/Batch/background pricing and behaviour, evals and fine-tuning availability. Note deprecations (Assistants API) with dates.

domains.name: Models & the Responses API
skills: Choose a GPT model and reasoning effort
Make Responses API requests; read output items; stream events
Know Chat Completions and the Assistants deprecation
Manage conversation state: manual, previous_response_id, conversations, retention

domains.name: Tools & Function Calling
skills: Define function tools and run the loop; parallel calls and tool_choice
Design good tools
Use built-in tools: web search, file search, code interpreter, computer use
Connect remote MCP servers; hosted vs your own tools

domains.name: Structured Outputs & Prompting
skills: Use Structured Outputs with JSON Schema and strict-mode rules; still validate
JSON mode vs Structured Outputs
Prompt reasoning models; instructions vs input; prompt objects and versioning

domains.name: Agents: SDK & Agents API
skills: Choose between the Responses API, Agents SDK and Agents API; decide if you need an agent
Build with the Agents SDK: agents, tools, handoffs, multi-agent
Add guardrails, human approval, sessions and tracing

domains.name: Evals, Cost & Production
skills: Cut cost and latency with prompt caching, Batch and background mode
Handle rate limits and retries
Run evals with graders before shipping; know when fine-tuning helps

domains.name: Safety & Security
skills: Defend against prompt injection, especially via tools and retrieved content
Use moderation; manage keys and data
Handle agent-specific risks: least privilege, approvals, sandboxing
